Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Rapidly enlarging upper-lip swelling beginning ~30 min after eating prawn soup at ~7 PM today; associated with increasing difficulty breathing, possible chest tightness, and dizziness.
- Timeline: Onset within 30 min of ingestion; progressive worsening at time of call.
- Past medical history:
  • Asthma (uses salbutamol inhaler).
  • Peanut allergy with probable anaphylaxis at age 6 (hospitalized; details unknown).
  • Similar episode of facial swelling and dyspnea after Chinese food ~1 year ago; self-managed with salbutamol only.
- Medications:
  • Salbutamol inhaler – dose/route/frequency not documented.
  • Antihistamines (unspecified) used intermittently for peanut allergy – dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Social history: Not discussed.
- Allergies:
  • Peanuts (anaphylactic reaction in past).

Objective:
- No formal physical examination performed (video consult).
- Patient reports:
  • Visible progressive upper-lip swelling (left corner initially, now whole upper lip).
  • Subjective airway tightness and breathing difficulty.
  • Dizziness.
- Vitals: Not obtained.
- Investigations: None.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Suspected anaphylaxis (trigger: prawn/shellfish)
   - Assessment: Acute anaphylactic reaction manifesting as angioedema, airway compromise, dizziness.
   - Differential diagnosis: Isolated angioedema, oral allergic syndrome, anxiety-related dyspnea.
   - Investigations planned: None pre-hospital; recommend hospital monitoring, serum tryptase (hospital protocol), specific IgE testing to shellfish/peanut at follow-up.
   - Treatment planned:
     • Immediate 999 ambulance activation (completed during call).
     • Instructed patient/mother to administer oral antihistamine while awaiting EMS.
     • Advised continuous observation until paramedics arrive.
     • Anticipate intramuscular epinephrine, airway support, IV fluids in ED.
   - Relevant referrals:
     • Post-discharge referral to allergy clinic for formal evaluation and prescription of epinephrine auto-injector.
     • Asthma review to optimize control and inhaler technique.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements: vitals, focused airway/skin/cardiorespiratory exam findings, medication reconciliation (doses/frequency), complete allergy list (drug/environmental), social history, family history.
● Internal conflicts: None noted; patient uncertain whether chest tightness is present.
● Transcript quality: Clear; minor background noise but all clinically relevant information intelligible.
